- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), overshooting by 2–5% in the following 3–5 days; apply dampening factor of 0.95–0.98 to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >75 and true is <72, reduce forecast by 2–4% in next period; if forecast <70 and true >72, increase by 2–4%.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error: if sentiment shifts sharply within 3 days, reduce forecast confidence by 10–20% and apply smoother decay to avoid overfitting.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
